answer: Clone Tax via Issuer Fee Split** Each identity must be sponsored by a distinct prior identity, which forfeits a fixed fee split across its own sponsors. Cloning forces the attacker to route sponsorship through a shrinking canyon of unrelated identities, each taking a cut. The fee schedule rises on a terrace: every new registration in a cohort pays more than the last, so mass registration front-loads cost. Like a tide, revenue returns to honest sponsors, funding their next fee. A marginal clone costs more than its expected yield.
